info.desc: A Moon Shaped Pool is the ninth studio album by the English rock band Radiohead, released as a download on 8 May 2016. The album's first two singles were "Burn the Witch" and "Daydreaming". CD and LP editions will be released by XL Recordings on 17 June 2016, followed in September by a "special edition" containing additional artwork and two bonus tracks. The album was produced by Nigel Godrich. Radiohead began work on A Moon Shaped Pool intermittently after finishing the 2012 tour for their previous album, 2011's The King of Limbs. Several songs on the album date back to .

podcast.body: Radiohead's latest album is noted for including content that has its roots in the earlier "Kid A" recording sessions. Specifically, its first single, "Burn the Witch," was conceived, composed, and partially recorded during that highly experimental and productive period, highlighting the long-term influence of the "Kid A" era on their later work. podcast.body: Recording for this album began in September 2014, two years after the tragic stage collapse in Toronto. The songs are notably presented in alphabetical order. Its release followed a straightforward, coordinated digital strategy through the band's website, iTunes, and, despite Thom Yorke's earlier reservations, streaming music sites, with a special edition physical version also made available. There were no interviews or advance road-testing of the songs; promotional hints came primarily through the band's website and social media, including commissioned short vignettes on Instagram. A notable controversy occurred on June 17, 2016, the day of the physical release, when a listening session at an indie record store in Istanbul, Turkey, was attacked by a gang who objected to music and beer being present during Ramadan, though fortunately no one was hurt. "Not a lot of razzle d'azza with this one, unless you count the fact that the songs are presented in alphabetical order."

podcast.body: This album, released in 2016, is part of Radiohead's independent projects, a model they adopted for all their work since 2008. They operate entirely on their own terms, having no use for the major label system anymore. "A Moon Shape Pool, which, like everything they've done since 2008, has been an independent project."
